KeyPassages: Exodus 10:26; Deuteronomy 14:6; Deuteronomy 14:7; Deuteronomy 14:8; Isaiah 5:28; Ezekiel 32:13
BiblicalUsage: Parsah is the hoof, the claw, the split foot. The law in Deuteronomy 14:6-8 names the clean animal by its hoof: it parts the hoof and chews the cud. In Exodus 10:26 Moses refuses to leave a hoof behind in Egypt, because the people must have animals to sacrifice. Isaiah 5:28 pictures the enemy's horses with hoofs like flint, and Ezekiel 32:13 says the waters will no longer be troubled by the hoof of beast or the foot of man.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God reads a hoof the way a farmer does, as the sign of what an animal is, and the law's small details are not small to Him. That is why I hold that not one hoof was left in Egypt: the sacrifice had to be whole, and so does my obedience.
